findings.problem: RouteWorkflow struct has no typestate or enum to prevent illegal state transitions; any code can set is_sent=true on a never-validated route
findings.failure_mode: A route that was never validated or marked for validation can be sent, violating the workflow invariant that only validated routes may transition to sent
findings.fix: Replace the flat struct with a typestate enum (e.g. RouteWorkflow<Unvalidated> -> RouteWorkflow<Validated> -> RouteWorkflow<Sent>) so invalid transitions are compile-time errors

findings.problem: status is a String instead of a domain enum; callers can set status to any arbitrary string ("foo", "", "SENT", null-like empty)
findings.failure_mode: The workflow state machine accepts arbitrary invalid statuses, making runtime state checks unreliable and impossible to exhaustively match on
findings.fix: Define `enum RouteStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }` and replace `pub status: String` with `pub status: RouteStatus`

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are independent booleans that allow impossible combinations: is_validated=false and is_sent=true
findings.failure_mode: The struct admits states like {status:"pending", is_validated:false, is_sent:true} which are logically inconsistent and represent a broken workflow invariant
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum or a single `RouteState { Unvalidated, Validated, Sent }` field that encodes the full lifecycle

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is Option<u64> that can be None while is_sent=true or status="sent", representing a partially-initialized sent state
findings.failure_mode: A route can be in the sent state without a timestamp, making audit trails and time-based queries produce incomplete or incorrect data
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the Sent variant of a typestate enum: `enum RouteState { Unvalidated, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain constraints; no validation that the identifier is well-formed, unique, or non-empty
findings.failure_mode: Empty strings, duplicate IDs, or non-route identifiers can be stored, violating domain invariants and enabling silent data corruption
findings.fix: Define `struct RouteId(String)` with a smart constructor `RouteId::new(s: &str) -> Result<RouteId, ParseError>` that rejects empty/invalid IDs

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts RouteWorkflow with raw String id, raw String status, and booleans; there is no parse boundary that validates inputs before the core logic consumes them, so callers can construct invalid domain states directly
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can bypass all workflow invariants by constructing a RouteWorkflow with any combination of fields, including is_sent=true with status="pending" and no validation
findings.fix: Replace the function signature with a fallible smart constructor that takes parsed inputs: `fn mark_sent(id: RouteId, validated_state: RouteState::Validated) -> Result<RouteState::Sent, TransitionError>` and remove the mutable struct mutation pattern

findings.problem: No error types exist; mark_sent returns RouteWorkflow instead of Result, so failures (if any) cannot be communicated to callers
findings.failure_mode: If a future transition requires validation checks (e.g. route not already sent), there is no error type to return; failures will be silently ignored or cause panics
findings.fix: Define `enum RouteError { AlreadySent, NotValidated, InvalidId(String) }` and return `Result<RouteState::Sent, RouteError>`

residual_risk: This is a structural/type-level review only. The codebase is a small synthetic fixture with 13 lines, but it fundamentally violates multiple Holzman laws: no typestate (make-illegal-states-unrepresentable), status String instead of enum, lifecycle booleans, optional lifecycle data outside variant, raw primitive id without newtype, no parse boundary, and no typed error taxonomy. These are architectural blockholders that no amount of testing can fix — the type system must enforce the invariants.
